subject: AWS Marketplace PrivateOffer onboarding & packaging options for DataSense
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@datasense.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 23:14:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace listing & PrivateOffer onboarding — DataSense

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the intro call earlier. We’re ready to get our AWS Marketplace listing live and would like to pursue a PrivateOffer so Procurement can sign under our contract terms. A few quick items from our side: 

- Procurement timeline: they want a PO in place by the end of next week (target 5/14).
- Packaging question: our infra team currently builds an AMI and a container image — curious whether you prefer an AMI for the listing or if a container/ECR-backed listing is acceptable for co-sell.
- Co-sell registration: want to understand what artifacts AWS needs from your side and what we should prepare (sales scripts, joint pitch deck).

Can you send a short onboarding checklist and any sample PO wording so our legal/procurement can review? Also happy to run a 30-min ops sync.

Best,
Rajiv
Director, Cloud Platform
DataSense Inc.

Attachments: none

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@datasense.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing & PrivateOffer onboarding — DataSense

Hi Rajiv — great to connect.

High level next steps from our side (we’ve attached the relevant docs):

1) Technical pack: we can accept either an AMI or container-based offering. For fastest time-to-listing + co-sell eligibility I recommend ECR/container images unless you have firm constraints requiring an AMI (we note AMI-based PrivateOffers sometimes need extra entitlements). See attached "ami-packaging-checklist.pdf" and the example listing copy.

2) Commercials: I attached a PO draft ("po-draft-DataSense.docx") with Redwood’s standard PrivateOffer terms. Procurement can sign and we’ll route the PrivateOffer via AWS for acceptance. If you need changes, flag the clauses and we’ll loop Legal.

3) Co-sell enablement: please share your preferred sales contacts and any pitch materials; we’ll prepare joint one-pager and register the deal with AWS. For registration we need: customer-facing items (pitch deck), high-level TCV, expected go-live date.

Proposed milestones:
- 5/11: ops sync (30 min) to confirm packaging and listing SKU mapping
- 5/13: final PO sign-off from DataSense
- 5/17: PrivateOffer submission to AWS and co-sell registration

Would 10am PT on 5/11 work for a quick call? I’ve cc’d Kimberly and Karthik to weigh in on technical packaging.

Thanks,
Olga
Partnerships Lead | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachments:
- po-draft-DataSense.docx (Commercial/PO template)
- ami-packaging-checklist.pdf (technical guidance)
- listing-copy-v1.html (draft product page)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing & PrivateOffer onboarding — DataSense

Thanks Olga — quick internal note on packaging (cc’ing Karthik for infra specifics):

- If DataSense can publish an ECR image (container) and we provide an AMI option as fallback, time-to-listing is usually shorter. Containers map cleanly to ECS/EKS deployments and avoid the AMI AMI-visibility entitlements.
- AMI path: if they insist on AMI we’ll need the image manifest, supported regions, and evidence of hardened build steps; that’s what the attached checklist covers. AMI PrivateOffers sometimes need additional AWS entitlements for marketplace billing mapping; AWS PMs can advise.
- SKU mapping: recommend two SKUs — pay-as-you-go (metered) and annual commit (PrivateOffer) so procurement can choose.

Karthik — can you confirm whether Redwood needs to run any pre-launch validation against their AMI network configs or if we can rely on their published ECR image?

-Kim

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@datasense.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing & PrivateOffer onboarding — DataSense

Hi all — following up from the ops sync this morning (thanks Rajiv for the time). Summary and action items: 

Summary:
- DataSense will proceed with ECR-based container images as primary listing artifact. They confirmed the ECR repo URI and image tags during the call.
- DataSense will also provide a pre-built AMI for regions where customers request AMI deployments; Redwood will store AMI metadata in the listing but won’t host AMIs.
- SKU plan: two SKUs (metered hourly and annual PrivateOffer). Procurement asked for the PrivateOffer PO by 5/14.

Action items (owners):
- DataSense (Rajiv): upload final listing copy to s3 and confirm ECR URI + IAM role for validation (due 5/12).
- DataSense (Procurement): review/initial-sign PO draft (po-draft-DataSense.docx) and return comments by 5/13.
- Redwood (Karthik): run a quick validation against the ECR image (smoke start + healthcheck) and confirm SKU metering dimensions (due 5/13).
- Redwood (Olga/Marissa): prepare co-sell one-pager and AWS deal registration pack (due 5/14).

Notes on validations:
- We will not require Redwood-managed AMI hosting. If an AMI is provided, we’ll ask for the AMI ID, region mapping, and a short checklist of installed agents for security review.

Next steps: Olga will send the final DocuSign/PrivateOffer link once PO is signed. I’ve attached the packaging checklist and a copy of the draft listing we reviewed.

Thanks — Karthik

Attachments referenced: ami-packaging-checklist.pdf, listing-copy-v1.html
